outputSections.label: Conventions Discovered
outputSections.content:
1. [category-visual-conformity] "Visual and structural language conforms to established category codes — the work looks like it belongs"
   Why it exists: Category recognition lowers cognitive processing load for evaluators; unfamiliar work triggers skepticism

2. [quality-is-differentiation] "Differentiation is achieved through quality improvement within conventions, not structural or positional deviation"
   Why it exists: Quality is the most legible and least-risk competitive strategy — requires no new mental model from evaluators

3. [evaluator-competence-frame] "The primary evaluator frame is competence — evaluators assess whether the work is done correctly"
   Why it exists: Risk-averse evaluation defaults to competence-checking before considering transformation potential

4. [narrative-setup-conflict-resolution] "Storytelling follows standard narrative arc — setup, conflict, resolution — for predictable evaluator comprehension"
   Why it exists: Cultural familiarity reduces cognitive effort; evaluators can follow without attention investment

5. [format-category-defaults] "Presentation format conforms to category defaults — duration, medium, pacing, delivery context"
   Why it exists: Format deviation requires additional cognitive work from evaluators — non-standard formats can signal amateurism

outputSections.label: Rule-Break Candidates
outputSections.content:

Convention: Visual and structural language conforms to established category codes — the work looks like it belongs
Proposed action: Abandon convention "category-visual-conformity" — replace [Use of dominant category visual language (palette, layout, typographic defaults)] with design language that directly signals "distinctive and memorable" for target audience.
Strategic value: POSITION-DRIVEN (strength: 1): Directly aligned with desired position "distinctive and memorable". Category vocabulary and evaluator-legible framing must be replaced.
Objective link: Breaking "category-visual-conformity" creates pattern disruption to serve the objective: "Create distinctive work in: General public and accountability advocates".
Break risk: Breaking visual category codes without deliberate positioning frames the work as simply unrecognised.

---

#2 [quality-is-differentiation] action:BREAK challenge-strength:1
Convention: Differentiation is achieved through quality improvement within conventions, not structural or positional deviation
Proposed action: Abandon convention "quality-is-differentiation" — replace [Higher production values; more refined execution of existing category codes] with design language that directly signals "distinctive and memorable" for target audience.
Strategic value: POSITION-DRIVEN (strength: 1): Directly aligned with desired position "distinctive and memorable". Superlatives within category language — 'the best', 'most refined', 'premium' must be replaced.
Objective link: Breaking "quality-is-differentiation" creates pattern disruption to serve the objective: "Create distinctive work in: General public and accountability advocates".
Break risk: Quality competition is a copying treadmill — structural differentiation is more durable.
